title: MCP — Audit health
description: Audit delivery health. The reference SLO is ZERO dropped audit records under normal load: any non-zero drop counter means the deployment is configured to violate the audit delivery guarantee, and that loudness is deliberately not suppressable.

panels.title: Dropped audit records (24h) — must be zero
panels.description: The single number this dashboard exists for. Any value above zero means records that should have been durably written were discarded because a buffer overflowed in drop mode. This is a configuration decision, not a transient — it does not resolve itself.

panels.title: Drop rate by sink
panels.description: Which sink is losing records. Broken out because a deployment may run a durable sink alongside a best-effort one, and only the durable one carries the guarantee.

panels.title: Append rate by sink and outcome
panels.description: Records written and whether the write succeeded. A failing append that is NOT accompanied by a drop means back-pressure is working — the dispatcher is being slowed rather than records being lost.

panels.title: Buffer depth by sink and instance
panels.description: A gauge sitting near its configured bound means dispatch is being back-pressured by audit. That is INTENDED behaviour under a slow sink — it is how the delivery guarantee is kept — but it is not a state to leave running, because request latency is paying for it.

panels.title: Append failure ratio
panels.description: Failed appends as a fraction of all appends. Rising here with a flat drop counter is the healthy failure mode; rising alongside drops is data loss in progress.
